findings.english_quote: He says, “Adultery and fornication, lawless drunkenness, wicked luxury, many foods, the extravagance of wealth, boasting, haughtiness and arrogance.
findings.issue: Paragraph 3 omits the shepherd’s imperative “Listen.” The list remains, but the source’s explicit instruction introducing it is absent.
findings.suggested_revision: Add “Listen.” at the beginning of the shepherd’s response, before “Adultery and fornication.” Review the revised response against the source before acceptance.

findings.issue: Paragraph 10 replaces the command to hear the things that follow with a declarative introduction. This drops the imperative addressed to Hermas rather than merely simplifying its vocabulary.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Next, listen to the things that follow:” and review that replacement against the selected source before acceptance.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all twelve paragraphs of the supplied working Greek. The standard edition has no identified concrete fidelity defect. The simplified edition retains the substantive teaching, lists, speaker division, necessity, negations, salvation language, and both concluding conditions, but omits two explicit listening commands. Both follow the reader-facing servant policy and disclose editorial supplements and substantive alternatives without replacing the selected working readings. Acceptance here concerns fidelity to the supplied source and disclosure; it does not authenticate the cited scans, unseen witnesses, or an exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
